rv.q: The dialogue alone is worth the price of the ticket and with a little help from dialect coach Carrie Hardin the cast's delivery is perfect.
City Lit has mounted a faithful production that offers a great opportunity to acquaint oneself with this classic play.
All the characters were played to great effect, in this writer’s opinion: Christy is equally confident in his storytelling and fearful of any possible retribution.
The finished product didn't grab me the way I hoped it might, but I certainly can't deny that the show was thoroughly realized by a talented and dedicated company.
If you take an interest in a script that is much too old-fashioned and if you have the will and ability to decipher heavy Irish brogue and its attendant vocabulary, then you will enjoy the show.

cn.t: City Lit Theatre's production of Synge's 1907 classic earns praise for its charming storytelling and intimate staging, with critics appreciating the historical comedy's twists and the company's handling of this controversial Irish tale.
